summary: A help box for an online bookstore's order page: a customer asks about their order and the answer streams in word by word, with a Stop button and a status line screen readers announce. The model call and its instructions live on the server, so the browser never sees the API key or the prompt. Worth asking about: the Try again button resends the wrong question, and the candidate wasn't sure how to recover from a dropped connection.

decisions.title: The model call and the system prompt stay on the server
decisions.why: The API key must never reach the browser, and the support instructions (who the assistant is, keep answers short) shouldn't be something a customer can edit in DevTools.
decisions.alternatives: Call the provider directly from the browser with a restricted key, or send the system prompt from the client with each request.
decisions.tradeoff: Every answer takes one extra hop through the app's server, and the server now handles streaming connections.

decisions.title: Pass chunks through as they arrive
decisions.why: Customers should see the first words in under a second instead of waiting for the whole answer; the proxy log shows a median of 354 ms to the first token.
decisions.alternatives: Wait for the full completion and return JSON, or use server-sent events with a message format.
decisions.tradeoff: Plain text streaming is simple, but it carries no structure: the client can't tell a finished answer from a cut-off one without extra signals.

decisions.title: Stop cancels the upstream request, not only the UI
decisions.why: When the customer presses Stop, the server aborts the call to the model, so no tokens are generated (and paid for) that nobody will read.
decisions.alternatives: Hide the rest of the answer in the browser and let the model finish in the background.
decisions.tradeoff: The partial answer is final; there is no way to resume it.

decisions.title: "Stopped" is a state of its own, not an error
decisions.why: The customer chose to stop, and the partial answer is still useful, so it stays on screen with a calm "Stopped" instead of an error message.
decisions.alternatives: Treat every aborted request as an error, or clear the answer on Stop.
decisions.tradeoff: One more state to handle; the retry path was the one that slipped (Try again sends the string "retry" instead of the customer's question).

questions: Try again sends the word "retry" instead of the customer's question. Walk me through how you'd fix it.
Why did you keep the system prompt on the server rather than sending it from the client?
What does a customer see if the connection drops halfway through an answer, and what should they see?
How would the client know an answer finished normally rather than being cut off?
Stop aborts the upstream call. What would you log to confirm that tokens really stop being generated?
The answer region has no label. How would a screen reader user find the answer after "Answering…"?
How would you add the order's real status (shipped, delayed) so the model doesn't guess?
What would you change if two questions were sent before the first answer finished?
How would you test this without calling the real model?
